question: Can the same pinned public Qwen3.5-2B Q4_K_M artifact execute through reproducible llama.cpp Vulkan offload on the authorized Galaxy S23 Ultra Adreno 740, with actual offload proven and CPU boundaries disclosed?

scope.included: Text-only inference through the same third-party Unsloth GGUF conversion on llama.cpp Vulkan0 / Adreno 740 with 25 model layers requested for GPU offload.
excluded: vision inputs or the vision encoder
CPU-only execution or Vulkan initialization followed by silent CPU fallback
a GPU-exclusive claim: CPU server/tokenizer/sampler/orchestration and unsupported-operation fallback remain possible and must be disclosed
NPU, QNN, HTP, or proprietary SDK execution
host measurements in the Android registry

upstream_model.name: Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B
upstream_model.architecture: 24-layer dense hybrid: three Gated DeltaNet layers followed by one full-attention layer, repeated six times
upstream_model.source: Pinned official model card and config.json. The official repository is Transformers-format source, not the deployed Android artifact.

deployment_artifact.source_kind: third-party GGUF conversion and quantization derived from Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B
deployment_artifact.format: GGUF v3, one self-contained shard, text model only

quantization.name: Q4_K_M
quantization.weight_scheme: GGML K-quant medium: primarily Q4_K block quantization with the Q4_K_M mixed tensor policy
quantization.block_scheme: Q4_K uses 256-weight super-blocks composed of 32-weight blocks with quantized scales/minima; the M variant retains selected tensors at higher precision according to the quantizer policy.
quantization.conversion_tool_revision_missing_reason: The pinned Unsloth repository and GGUF metadata identify Unsloth, Q4_K_M, and the importance matrix but do not publish the exact converter/quantizer commit. Artifact bytes are still bound by revision, size, and SHA-256; this provenance limitation must remain visible.

tokenizer_and_template.template_difference: The deployed template changes only iteration over tool-call argument mappings. The canonical system+user, no-tools branch is unaffected; canonical rendered bytes are independently hash-bound.

thinking.proof:
Every canonical rendered prompt must end with the exact bytes <think>

</think>

. A nonempty thinking prefix is a fatal mismatch.

route_rationale.chosen: Pinned public llama.cpp Vulkan backend using the same already viable Qwen3.5-2B Q4_K_M GGUF isolates backend effects while avoiding model or quantization changes.
route_rationale.offload_claim_boundary: The route may be called Vulkan GPU offload only when the device log proves Vulkan0 on Adreno 740, a Vulkan model buffer, a Vulkan compute buffer, and all 25/25 offloadable model layers offloaded. CPU retains server, tokenizer, sampler, graph scheduling/orchestration, and any operation unsupported by Vulkan. The route is not GPU-exclusive.
tradeoffs: The deployment artifact and quantization remain third-party, not official Qwen artifacts.
Vulkan is public and reproducible but Android uses the device vendor Vulkan driver.
The pinned NDK glslc cannot compile optional cooperative-matrix, integer-dot, bfloat16, or FP4 shader extensions, so only the generated base shader variants are embedded.
Runtime and quantization differ from other model routes, so family comparisons are confounded.
route_rationale.fallback_policy: Any missing Adreno/Vulkan/offloaded-layer/model-buffer/compute-buffer proof, GPU option ignored warning, Vulkan initialization failure, or CPU-only result is a blocker rather than publishable GPU evidence.

runtime.name: llama.cpp

shader_sources.embedding: The pinned vulkan-shaders-gen host tool invokes the pinned NDK glslc and embeds generated SPIR-V arrays into the static ggml-vulkan backend.

runtime.build: CMake Release, GGML_VULKAN=ON, static llama/GGML and c++_static; Android libvulkan/libm/libdl/libc remain dynamic. Embedded SPIR-V is generated at build time with pinned NDK glslc. Source/build paths are prefix-mapped; OpenSSL and embedded web UI are disabled.
runtime.greedy_proof: temperature=-1 is normalized to zero in the server generation settings. At the pinned revision, src/llama-sampler.cpp:270-282 retains only the highest-logit token whenever temperature <= 0; the request sampler chain contains only temperature and all penalties are neutral.
runtime.state_reset: The loaded llama-server Vulkan route and slot/session object remain alive. Before every logical request, POST /slots/0?action=erase must succeed and its duration is recorded separately outside total-request timing. Each completion sets cache_prompt=false; timings.cache_n must equal zero, prompt_n the full independently tokenized prompt count, and prompt_ms positive.

shader_compiler_variants.source: Ubuntu 24.04 archive packages glslc 2023.8-1build1 and libshaderc1 2023.8-1build1

device.phone_lock: artifacts/locks/phone.lock held across identity, staging, execution, evidence, and cleanup

timing_and_evidence.setup_boundary: Host monotonic timestamp immediately before remote Vulkan llama-server launch through health readiness plus required backend-proof observation; includes artifact mapping, Vulkan device/runtime/pipeline initialization, model/context creation, and readiness polling.
timing_and_evidence.request_boundary: Immediately before native template rendering through final streamed stop delivery. The separately timed slot erase completes before this boundary and is not included in total request.
timing_and_evidence.request_to_first_token: Client request start through the first SSE event carrying a generated token ID.
timing_and_evidence.prefill: llama.cpp final-event prompt_ms and prompt_n; route-internal prompt evaluation timing.
timing_and_evidence.post_prefill_to_first_token: Null because llama.cpp does not expose a server-clock first-token timestamp alignable with aggregate prompt_ms.
timing_and_evidence.decode: External first generated-token event through final stop event, with the first token excluded from the numerator; llama.cpp predicted timing is retained separately and includes all generated tokens.
timing_and_evidence.memory: 100 ms target sampling of process PSS/VmHWM plus public KGSL busy/frequency sysfs nodes over the server lifecycle. Process memory includes CPU-visible allocations but does not directly isolate vendor-driver/GPU-private allocations.

fatal_gates: wrong workload, model, runtime, runner, device, or staged hash
missing all 25/25 layers offloaded, Vulkan model buffer, or Vulkan compute buffer proof
GPU option ignored, Vulkan initialization failure, or CPU-only fallback evidence
prompt plus 2048 ceiling exceeds 8192, or server reports truncation
non-thinking template control or greedy sampler configuration not applied
slot erase fails, timings.cache_n is nonzero, or full prompt evaluation is unproved
unauthorized/destructive device operation or phone-lock violation
raw output cannot be bound to the claimed request
nullable_not_fatal: individual thermal sensors unavailable to shell
KGSL frequency/busy telemetry unavailable to Android shell when server-log offload proof is complete
brief memory or GPU-activity peaks missed by 100 ms target sampling
exact partition of individual graph operations between Vulkan and CPU when the route is described only as bounded GPU offload, not GPU-exclusive execution

blocked_result.next_decision: Whether to authorize a separately named, pinned public llama.cpp OpenCL/Adreno investigation without changing model, quantization, or workload.
